capability_summaries.name: Conditional Access
capability_summaries.outcome: Decide who can sign in, from where, on which devices, and whether they must prove it is really them (for example with multi-factor authentication).
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Passwords alone are not enough. Good sign-in rules stop many everyday account takeovers before damage is done.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Your licenses include advanced sign-in rules, but they may still be loose or incomplete.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P2
capability_summaries.plain_name: Deep protection and visibility on PCs and devices
capability_summaries.outcome: See attacks on laptops and servers in more detail, find weak software, and respond before a single infected PC becomes a company-wide problem.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Devices are where people work. If they are not enrolled in advanced protection, you are flying partly blind.
capability_summaries.if_unused: You may be paying for advanced device protection on seats that are not fully enrolled.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender for Identity
capability_summaries.plain_name: Watchdogs on your on-site directory (if you still have one)
capability_summaries.outcome: Spot attackers moving through traditional office servers and Active Directory, not only cloud sign-ins.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Many organizations still rely on on-site domain controllers. Cloud-only tools cannot see every attack path there.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Identity threat sensors may be missing or unhealthy, so on-site directory attacks stay invisible.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 P2
capability_summaries.plain_name: Stronger email and file threat protection
capability_summaries.outcome: Open risky attachments and links in a safe way, catch advanced phishing, and investigate email threats faster when something slips through.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Most business breaches still start with email. Better email protection reduces ransomware and invoice fraud.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Extra email protections in your license may still be off, in test mode, or only covering a few people.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Entra ID P2
capability_summaries.outcome: Give people powerful admin rights only when they need them, and get better tools to catch risky sign-ins on high-value accounts.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Admin accounts are the keys to your email, files, and business apps. If one is stolen, an attacker can look like a trusted employee.
capability_summaries.if_unused: You are paying for stronger admin protections that are not fully turned on yet.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Entra ID Protection
capability_summaries.plain_name: Alerts when a sign-in looks suspicious
capability_summaries.outcome: Automatically spot odd sign-in behavior (impossible travel, leaked passwords, unfamiliar locations) and require extra proof or block access.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Attackers often use valid passwords. Risk detection helps catch the session even when the password was correct.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Suspicious-sign-in protection is included in your plan but may not be enforcing anything yet.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Sentinel
capability_summaries.plain_name: A central security command center in the cloud
capability_summaries.outcome: Bring security signals together in one place, detect patterns humans miss, and automate parts of incident response.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Without a place that correlates events, teams drown in alerts from many products and miss the story that ties them together.
capability_summaries.if_unused: A security workspace may exist, but few detections or smart analytics are turned on.

capability_summaries.name: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
capability_summaries.plain_name: Guardrails so sensitive data is harder to leak
capability_summaries.outcome: Warn or block people when they try to share credit cards, health data, or other sensitive information in the wrong place.
capability_summaries.why_it_matters: Accidental oversharing is common. Guardrails protect customers and reduce regulatory and reputational harm.
capability_summaries.if_unused: Data-protection rules may be missing or still in "test only" mode, so nothing is enforced yet.

findings.title: Identity Protection policies off or report-only
findings.summary: No Conditional Access policies with user-risk or sign-in-risk conditions were found (Identity Protection not operationalized via CA).
findings.remediation: Enable user-risk and sign-in-risk policies in staged rollout, then enforce for privileged and high-value users.
findings.customer_title: Suspicious sign-ins may not be blocked automatically
findings.customer_summary: We did not find automatic responses when Microsoft marks a sign-in or account as risky. That protection may still be turned off.
findings.customer_next_step: Turn on risk-based sign-in protection in stages — start by requiring extra verification when Microsoft marks a sign-in as risky.

findings.title: PIM licensed but privileged access not operationalized
findings.summary: Found 4 standing privileged role assignment(s) and 0 PIM eligible schedules — just-in-time admin access is not in use.
findings.remediation: Convert standing admin roles to PIM-eligible where possible, require activation with MFA/justification, and review permanent role assignments.
findings.customer_title: Admin accounts still have "always on" superpowers
findings.customer_summary: Admin superpowers appear permanently on. Time-limited admin access (included in your stronger identity plan) does not look like it is being used.
findings.customer_next_step: Ask IT to turn on time-limited admin access for your top admins first (Global Administrator and similar roles).

findings.title: Defender for Endpoint licensed seats vs onboarded devices gap
findings.summary: Large Defender for Endpoint onboarding gap: 40 onboarded vs ~100 licensed units (40%).
findings.remediation: Onboard missing devices via Intune, GPO, or scripts; investigate unhealthy sensors; align license assignment with actual endpoints.
findings.customer_title: Some PCs may not be enrolled in advanced device protection
findings.customer_summary: You appear to pay for advanced device protection on many seats, but relatively few devices are enrolled.
findings.customer_next_step: Compare licensed seats to enrolled devices and enroll the missing ones (often through your device management tools).

findings.title: Dormant privileged identities still enabled
findings.summary: Found 2 enabled privileged user(s) with no successful sign-in in the last 90 days (of 4 privileged principal(s)).
findings.remediation: Disable or archive unused privileged accounts, remove unneeded role assignments, and prefer just-in-time access via PIM.
findings.customer_title: Powerful accounts that nobody uses are still switched on
findings.customer_summary: Some powerful accounts are still switched on but have not been used recently. Unused admin accounts are a favorite target for attackers.
findings.customer_next_step: Review enabled admin accounts that have not signed in for a long time; disable or remove access you no longer need.

findings.title: Purview DLP licensed but not enforced in production
findings.summary: Secure Score suggests DLP is largely unused (2 controls, ~10% completion).

evidence.note: Uses Microsoft Secure Score DLP/information-protection controls as a proxy when direct Purview policy APIs are unavailable to the app.

findings.remediation: Deploy core DLP policies for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and endpoints; move from simulation to enforce after tuning.
findings.customer_title: Guardrails against accidental data leaks may not be active
findings.customer_summary: You appear to pay for data-leak protection that is not meaningfully enforced yet.
findings.customer_next_step: Start with a simple policy for email and cloud files that detects obvious sensitive data, then move from "test" to "enforce" after a short tuning period.

findings.title: Sentinel UEBA / entity analytics not enabled
findings.summary: Sentinel UEBA / entity analytics does not appear enabled.
findings.remediation: Enable Entity behavior analytics (UEBA) on the Sentinel workspace and ensure required data sources are connected.
findings.customer_title: Behavior-based detection may still be switched off
findings.customer_summary: Behavior analytics that learn normal patterns for people and devices still looks switched off.
findings.customer_next_step: Ask your security admin to turn on behavior analytics (UEBA) in the security workspace and connect the main data sources it needs.

findings.title: Privileged sign-ins not strongly gated by Conditional Access
findings.summary: Conditional Access is partially configured: missing enforced legacy authentication block (report-only legacy block exists).
findings.remediation: Create CA policies that require phishing-resistant MFA for privileged roles and block legacy authentication tenant-wide where possible.
findings.customer_title: Powerful accounts may sign in without strong extra checks
findings.customer_summary: Some sign-in protections are present, but the full set is not enforced yet (multi-factor authentication and/or blocking outdated sign-in methods).
findings.customer_next_step: Require multi-factor authentication for admins and block legacy email sign-in methods that skip modern security prompts.

findings.title: Defender for Office 365 P2 policies not broadly enforced
findings.summary: Secure Score shows partial MDO-related control completion (3 controls, ~45%). Safe Links/Attachments may be incomplete or not fully enforced.

controls.description: Safe Links is enabled for email
Safe Attachments not fully rolled out

evidence.note: Uses Microsoft Secure Score control signals as a proxy for Defender for Office 365 policy enforcement when direct policy APIs are unavailable.

findings.remediation: Enforce Safe Attachments and Safe Links for all recipients; enable preset security policies or equivalent custom policies in block mode.
findings.customer_title: Extra email protections may not cover everyone yet
findings.customer_summary: Some stronger email protections appear configured, but not fully. Safe Links and Safe Attachments may still miss people or stay in test mode.
findings.customer_next_step: Turn on the recommended email security policies for all users (not just a test group), starting with safe links and safe attachments.

findings.title: Sentinel workspace with thin analytics rule coverage
findings.summary: Thin Sentinel analytics coverage: 2 enabled scheduled/NRT rule(s), 2 tactic(s) (total rules=3).
findings.remediation: Enable relevant content hub solutions and scheduled rules; cover identity, endpoint, and cloud control-plane sources first.
findings.customer_title: Your security command center may have few alarms turned on
findings.customer_summary: Some detection alarms are on, but coverage still looks light for a paid security command center.
findings.customer_next_step: Enable a starter set of detection rules for sign-ins, email, and devices, then expand coverage with your IT or security partner.

findings.title: Defender for Identity licensed but sensors missing or unhealthy
findings.summary: No Defender for Identity–related Secure Score controls were found. Cannot confirm sensor deployment from this signal alone.

evidence.note: Defender for Identity sensor health is approximated from Secure Score controls when the MDI API is not configured.

findings.remediation: Deploy and health-check MDI sensors on all DCs; fix connectivity and directory service account configuration issues.
findings.customer_title: On-site directory servers may lack attack sensors
findings.customer_summary: We could not confirm whether on-site directory attack sensors are installed. If you still run office domain controllers, ask IT to verify.
findings.customer_next_step: Confirm whether you still use on-site directory servers; if yes, install and health-check the identity sensors on each one.

recommended_next_steps: Turn on risk-based sign-in protection in stages — start by requiring extra verification when Microsoft marks a sign-in as risky.
Ask IT to turn on time-limited admin access for your top admins first (Global Administrator and similar roles).
Compare licensed seats to enrolled devices and enroll the missing ones (often through your device management tools).
Review enabled admin accounts that have not signed in for a long time; disable or remove access you no longer need.
Start with a simple policy for email and cloud files that detects obvious sensitive data, then move from "test" to "enforce" after a short tuning period.
